_comment: Extension fixture set for bucket bc6b90e2 (src/swarm/agents.py).
WHY THIS EXISTS. bc6b90e2 carries 8 fixtures in echoswarm_qa.json, and four
nominally-similar distill configs scored 1/8, 2/8, 4/8 and 5/8 on it. A spread
of 4 on an 8-item test means no claim in the cartridge track survives its own
noise floor. Standard error falls as 1/sqrt(n), so tripling the item count is
the cheapest real fix — better than any further recipe tuning.
DELIBERATELY A SEPARATE FILE. Appending to echoswarm_qa.json would change the
denominator of every historical number (7/25, 10/25, 5/13) and destroy
comparability with the logged results. Pass --fixtures to the eval to use it.
EVERY ANSWER IS IN THE KEPT VERBATIM. The 4096-char cap discards part of some
buckets, and five of the original 25 fixtures are structurally unanswerable
because their keywords live in discarded text or in the wrong bucket. These
were written against the actual distilled text and are checked by

fixtures.question: What are the four agent types defined in the AgentType enum?
What are the five states an agent can be in?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: WAITING, INFORMED, EVACUATING, SAFE and STRANDED.

fixtures.question: What state is an IMMOBILE agent placed in as soon as it is constructed?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: __post_init__ sets an IMMOBILE agent's state to STRANDED immediately.

fixtures.question: In which agent states does receive_message refuse the message and return False?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: It returns False for IMMOBILE agents and for agents already EVACUATING, SAFE or STRANDED.

fixtures.question: What does an agent do the first time it receives a message while WAITING?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: It stores the tokens and hop_count and moves from WAITING to INFORMED.

fixtures.question: How does an Agent stop the same neighbour being counted twice as a confirmation?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: It keeps a _seen_sources set and ignores any source_id already in it, so only distinct sources count.

fixtures.question: In which states does relay_tokens return None instead of broadcasting?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: relay_tokens returns None when the agent is WAITING, STRANDED or SAFE, and for IMMOBILE agents.

fixtures.question: How many tokens does a SKEPTICAL agent drop before relaying, and how are they chosen?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: It pops exactly one random key token from the list before relaying.

fixtures.question: What are the default values of hop_count, ticks_informed and confirmations on a new Agent?
What does the route field on an Agent hold?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: A pre-computed node path to the shelter, with route_index tracking the current step.

fixtures.question: Which base classes do the AgentType and AgentState enums inherit from?
Does a PANIC agent wait for confirmations before it relays?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: No — a PANIC agent relays immediately, unlike SKEPTICAL which waits for 2 confirmations.

fixtures.question: What is the default state of a newly constructed Agent that is not IMMOBILE?
What does receive_message return when it accepts a message from a new source?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: True, indicating this was a new confirmation.

fixtures.question: What parameter does the evacuating agent's can_act method take, and what does it return?
Which state transition does can_act decide?
fixtures.ground_truth_answer: Whether the agent should move from INFORMED to EVACUATING.
